_comment: Which hosts a Markdown reader may fetch images from without asking (MarkdownDocumentView with showsImages, first used by StoryMaker's Read view, 2026-10-03). Opening a chapter must not ping an arbitrary server: an image from any host not listed here renders as a link instead, the way mail readers hold back remote images. Local files always load. Content, so a host is added by PR with no rebuild. thumb.wikimedia.org added 2026-10-04: the Commons API now returns its scaled copies (thumburl) from that host, so four of the pilot's six pictures rendered as links. Seattle city feeds added 2026-10-11 (spdblotter, fireline, sdotblog .seattle.gov): the Seattle Local News routine shows up to two photos from the city's own feeds, credited and linked to the story; the iPhone's AI Write reader now loads pictures under these same rules. Neighborhood outlets serve photos from shared CDNs (i0.wp.com, S3) and are deliberately NOT listed — trusting a CDN host trusts every site on it. 2026-10-11: the archives the Black Seattle book's portraits come from (UW Libraries Digital Collections, BlackPast, HistoryLink, archive.org): the author's rule is that every history opens with its subject's portrait, and from an unlisted host StoryMaker showed a link where the face should be. 2026-10-28: the morning news routines (Seattle Local News, AI Daily) show each story's own picture, so the outlets they read are listed by the host their pictures come from. The rule stays: a host only that publisher serves from (its own domain, its own CDN or bucket name: images.seattletimes.com, westseattleblog-assets.s3.amazonaws.com, media.tegna-media.com for KING 5, npr.brightspotcdn.com for KNKX). Never a host anyone can serve through: i0.wp.com (the routines use the outlet's own copy instead), storage.ghost.io, storage.googleapis.com, images.ctfassets.net, substackcdn.com, cdn-uploads.huggingface.co, github.com, a bare s3.amazonaws.com. Outlets on those simply run without pictures.
